issues.description: Ingest clears warnings/stats but never clears stale results, so removed or invalidated source rows remain in the database.
Ingest accepts a nonexistent or wrong input directory and silently creates an empty database instead of failing fast.
Harness B parsing assumes JSON lines and metrics are objects, so valid JSON arrays/scalars or malformed metrics crash ingest.
Missing Harness B id/model/benchmark fields become empty strings, allowing silent row collisions and data loss.
Harness A rows with empty run_id, model, or task are accepted rather than warned/skipped, producing bad canonical data.
XML parsing is unguarded, so malformed XML crashes ingest and untrusted XML can expose denial-of-service risk.
Ingest is not atomic; stats are cleared before parsing and row upserts commit incrementally, leaving partial state after failures.
Duplicate run IDs for sources A and C silently overwrite existing rows while only Harness B duplicates are counted.
Report opens through connect(), which initializes and mutates a database path instead of using read-only report behavior.
Fixture generation recursively deletes any user-supplied target directory without guardrails.
Tests only cover generated fixtures and miss malformed input, stale re-ingest, empty identifiers, missing dirs, and atomic failure cases.
